note: Compiled on 19 October 2026 from the public repository's history; it was not published alongside each release. Each entry links to its commit on main or to the pull request that published it, where the merge commit is shown. Counts are those of data/evidence.json and data/ontology.json in that version; for registry versions the date is the registry's as-of date. Corrections changed content that had already been published; pre-release review fixes were made before a version was merged and were never published.

entries.title: Registry v0.7.0: the online-services ranking corrected, JAZARI general assemblies and a per-institute operational-evidence gap
changes: Two records, each read in full from its source: the ministry's release on the general assemblies of four JAZARI institutes held on 8 September 2026 (MAI-EV-0048), and the official Digital Morocco 2030 brochure (MAI-EV-0049).

The general assemblies are recorded as a governance event in the status of JAZARI ROOT, EduTech, Industrie X.0 and Smart City. No stage changed: a general assembly, and the ministry's description of a move to operational implementation, are not operation.

Evidence gap GAP-07 asks which JAZARI institutes have documented governance, staff, premises, operational activity or outputs. It is assessed per institute (ROOT, EduTech, Industrie X.0, Smart City, Nador) across eight evidence dimensions, with three published resolution paths that keep documented operation, documented non-commencement and documented discontinuation after operation apart; an institute that meets none has an unknown operational status. A legal approval, a governance event or missing records cannot resolve an institute, an institute that never operated is not recorded as discontinued, and an institute can be resolved while the others stay open. The validator and the example consumer check these rules.
GAP-06 re-assessed against the brochure; it remains open.

Not changed: the further ROOT signatories named in Bulletin Officiel 7534 are not added. The summary makes the State the party, represented by the undersigned officeholders (one of them the president of the CNDP, acting on the State's side); the signatory_of relationship has no published definition that distinguishes signing as the State's representative from signing as a party, so adding them would present each ministry and the CNDP as a contracting party in its own right.
corrections: The Digital Morocco 2030 ranking objective (113th to 50th) was described as the e-government development index (EGDI), following the national news agency's dispatch, and compared with Morocco's overall EGDI ranks. The strategy's own brochure defines it as the United Nations Online Services Index (OSI), a component of the EGDI, with 113th as the 2022 position. MAI-EV-0002, MAI-EV-0046, GAP-06 and the Digital Morocco 2030 summary now keep the strategy's claimed OSI position, the United Nations' OSI values (which come without a rank) and the overall EGDI ranks apart. The 113th OSI place is the strategy's figure and has not been verified.
MAI-EV-0008 said the Bulletin Officiel text approving the JAZARI ROOT convention had not been located; it now points to MAI-EV-0047, which records it.
MAI-EV-0047 said that no act concerns the Al Jazari institute in Nador; the statement is now limited to Bulletin Officiel 7534 and does not imply that no other act exists.

entries.title: Registry v0.6.0: legal establishment of four JAZARI institutes, Toubkal workloads, infrastructure signings and the e-government index
changes: Six records, each read in full from its source: the Bulletin Officiel joint orders approving the founding conventions of JAZARI ROOT, EduTech, Industrie X.0 and Smart City (MAI-EV-0047); the ministry's release on the Nexus AI Factory memorandum (MAI-EV-0044); the convention launching studies for the Igoudar Dakhla green data-centre programme (MAI-EV-0045); the United Nations e-government index for Morocco (MAI-EV-0046); the GemMaroc preprint (MAI-EV-0042); and a genomic language model trained on Toubkal (MAI-EV-0043).

The eight recorded signatures of the JAZARI ROOT and JAZARI Industrie X.0 conventions now also cite the gazette, so they no longer rest only on announcements and leave GAP-05, which now lists 11 of the 33 relationships that assert a formal act instead of 19; the signed texts are still not recorded.
The signatures of the Nexus AI Factory memorandum by the ministry and Nexus Core Systems are now VERIFIED FACT on the ministry's own release, instead of announced plans reported by the press.
GAP-03, GAP-04 and GAP-06 re-assessed against the new records; all six gaps remain open. No lifecycle stage changed: legal establishment, a memorandum and the launch of studies are not operation.
Evidence type official_gazette added for Bulletin Officiel texts; like a procurement notice, it cannot evidence a lifecycle stage or use.
Excerpts in Arabic are marked right-to-left on the evidence pages.
corrections: The registry attributed the GemMaroc fine-tuning runs to "Belkasmi et al.", copying the Toubkal article; that article's own reference is the GemMaroc preprint by Skiredj et al., and the preprint does not say where the runs were made. The Toubkal attribute, MAI-EV-0041 and GAP-03 now say so.

The Digital Morocco 2030 ranking objective's starting point of 113th is now noted as the source's figure: no United Nations edition ranks Morocco 113th; it ranked 101st in 2022 and 90th in 2024. (Corrected in v0.7.0: those are overall EGDI ranks, while the strategy defines its ranking as the Online Services Index component; see the v0.7.0 corrections.)
The status of JAZARI Smart City and JAZARI EduTech said that no founding convention was documented; their founding conventions were approved in July 2026.
review_fixes: GAP-03 attributed to the GemMaroc preprint a total of about 58 GPU-hours, which is the Toubkal article's table of the runs; the preprint reports about 48 GPU-hours for its longest run, which GAP-03 now gives.
Statements that signed texts are "not published" replaced by what the cited sources reproduce and what this registry has obtained; GAP-04 re-assessed for the Nexus relationship notes, and still open.
MAI-EV-0044 quotes the release's MAD 12 billion "investissement initial … mobilisé sur deux phases" and notes that it does not establish any expenditure.

GAP-05, the Q8 answer, the matrix and the definition of includes-non-announcement-record distinguish the eight signatures that also cite the gazette's approval from those resting on official reports; a qualification marks matrix rows citing an official gazette record.

The GAP-06 statement on the 113th starting point also cites the strategy record it comes from (MAI-EV-0002); MAI-EV-0047 names JAZARI EduTech and JAZARI Smart City; MAI-EV-0030 notes that the ministry release it could not retrieve is now MAI-EV-0044.

entries.title: Registry v0.5.0: evidence basis of signatures, Q8 scope and Digital Morocco 2030 progress
changes: Evidence gap GAP-06: measured progress towards the official targets of Digital Morocco 2030, assessed against its four existing records. Every strategy with an official target now has a gap on its progress, which the build checks; Q9 no longer reports a target as not assessed.

Every relationship shown as Signed now states that the signing is documented by a report of it and that the signed text is not recorded in this registry; a new evidence type, signed_instrument, is reserved for a record of a signed text that the registry has read in full, from a party or an official publisher, with the instrument's title, date and signatories; a report of a signing never qualifies. No record has that type.
Q8 states the kinds and stages of the projects it counts.
The consumer example reads the documentation-basis names from matrix.json instead of fixing them in its code.

The relationship from Morocco AI 2030 to the JAZARI network now notes that it records the ministry's description of how the roadmap is to be implemented, not documented implementation; GAP-02 was re-assessed against it, with no change to its text.
No record, entity or relationship was added or changed, and no classification or stage changed.
breaking_changes: matrix.json rows[].documentation_basis: the value includes-formal-record is renamed includes-non-announcement-record, for the same rows. A consumer comparing with the old value fails, as the v0.4.1 example consumer does (exit status 1). No alias is provided. Migration notes are on /data/ and in the manifest (breaking_changes).
corrections: The documentation basis includes-formal-record (matrix.json, v0.4.1) is renamed includes-non-announcement-record: the records it covers are official reports, repositories, rankings and observations, none of which is a signed text, so for signatures the name suggested an instrument that is not recorded. The matrix page and the GAP-05 text no longer imply that the instrument is recorded for relationships outside GAP-05.

The JAZARI network's status said that signed founding instruments are documented for JAZARI ROOT and JAZARI Industrie X.0, and two record notes said the same; the registry records reported signings, not the signed texts. The registry index called JAZARI ROOT the network's core institute without saying it is planned. No JAZARI institute's stage changed: all remain announced.

The Q8 question said "documented AI or computing projects"; it now says "the AI-related and computing projects recorded in this registry", since 8 of its 12 projects are announced and one is a catalogue platform rather than an AI system.

entries.title: Registry v0.4.1: published data documented and independently verifiable
changes: A data reference page (/data/) describing the published files, identifiers, provenance, null and absent values, versions, coverage limits and which parts of Q8 and Q9 can be recomputed from the data.
A manifest (/data/manifest.json) listing each published JSON file with its SHA-256, so that a consumer can tell whether the files it fetched belong to the same build.

matrix.json and the published gaps.json now carry the rules used to derive them, including row order, the caveats added to each row, the gap checks and the digest algorithm; data/gaps.json defines its states; the manifest lists the values accepted for source type, evidence type and status basis.

An example consumer (/examples/registry_consumer.py, Python standard library only) that checks the published data and recomputes the matrix, the gap checks and digests, and the reproducible parts of Q8 and Q9.

Evidence cards no longer extend past narrow screens when a quotation contains a long unbroken string, including while web fonts load or when they are blocked; the homepage navigation fits a 320-pixel screen.
No record, entity or relationship was added or changed.
corrections: ontology.json carried version 0.3.0 and as-of date 18 October 2026 in v0.4.0, although its content had changed in that version; it now carries the registry version and date, and the validator requires both files to agree.
The registry index said the registry did not yet cover AI companies, models or datasets, which it has covered since v0.2.0.

The definition of the operational stage in ontology.json said it was documented "by a source independent of announcements", which could be read as requiring an independent source; it now states that the record may be an observation of the operator's live service, an operator's report of use or an independent source, and that public availability is not evidence of use. The announced stage's definition now says delivery is not documented in this registry, rather than that there is no evidence of it.

entries.title: Registry v0.4.0: institutional matrix and evidence gaps
changes: Institutional evidence matrix: each organisation's and initiative's documented relationships, with classification, the related entity's status, sources and qualifications, also as matrix.json.
Evidence gap register: five open questions, with what the registry establishes, what it does not and what would resolve each, also as gaps.json; gaps are re-checked against the data on every build.
Questions Q8 (organisations and projects) and Q9 (official targets and recorded progress).

Two records: the ministry's presentation of the Maroc IA 2030 roadmap's main advances (MAI-EV-0040), and a peer-reviewed article on Toubkal reporting large-language-model fine-tuning, written by authors affiliated with its host university (MAI-EV-0041).

entries.title: Registry v0.3.0: AI deployment evidence
changes: Rules for operational and pilot claims: the basis must be stated, the operator named separately from any provider or developer, and outcomes are never recorded as facts.
First AI application recorded as operational (Idarati AI), on the basis of public availability only; use is not documented.
Health and financial-services entries, recorded as announced.
Questions page: deployments, operators, evidence recency, unresolved entries.
A separate source checker that re-fetches sources without changing data.
corrections: DeepEcho software changed from in development (published in v0.2.0) to unresolved: the FDA record contradicts the company website's disclaimer, which no longer sets a stage and is marked superseded.
review_fixes: FDA wording limited to 510(k) clearance, and the applicant's link to the Moroccan company recorded as an association, not a legal identity.
A provider attribution for Idarati AI (Berexia) removed: the label appears only in interface text and is not shown on the assistant.

entries.title: Registry v0.2.0: companies, models, datasets and lifecycle stages
changes: AI companies, open models and datasets, and compute infrastructure.
Lifecycle stages for projects, models and datasets, each backed by a record that declares the stage.
First version of the questions page.
corrections: The higher-education ministry, recorded in v0.1.0 as involved in the Nador memorandum, recorded as a signatory on a new source naming the signatories.
review_fixes: The DarijaBERT developer link classified as independent analysis: the model card names "AIOX Lab", and identification is by name.
UM6P Ventures' origin set to unresolved; Toubkal recorded as compute infrastructure, not as an AI application.

entries.title: Registry v0.1.0: evidence registry, ontology and quality gates
changes: Evidence registry and ontology with claim classifications, a validator and automated quality gates.
Generated registry pages, an independence statement on every page and self-hosted fonts.
corrections: Unsourced claims, rules that were not true of the site and placeholder links on the original homepage removed or corrected.
review_fixes: The CNDP recorded as listing Law 09-08 in its regulatory framework, not as administering it.
Conventions signed for the creation of Jazari institutes not presented as constituted institutions.
